entities.name: PLAAT4 (Q9UL19)
observations: The 164-aa query exactly matches reviewed human phospholipase A and acyltransferase 4 (UniProt Q9UL19).
Curated annotation reports calcium-independent PLA1/PLA2 hydrolysis of glycerophospholipid acyl esters, with PLA1 generally stronger, plus O- and N-acyltransferase activities.
N-acyltransferase activity transfers an acyl group from phosphatidylcholine or other glycerophospholipid to phosphatidylethanolamine, forming N-acylphosphatidylethanolamine (NAPE).

entities.name: Glycerophospholipid deacylation
observations: PLA1 hydrolysis example: 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine + H2O → 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine + fatty acid + H(+), Rhea RHEA:15801.
PLA2 hydrolysis can release the fatty acid from the other glycerol position, yielding the corresponding lysophospholipid; Rhea RHEA:18689.
